items.ask: What is the tallest tree in the world?

explain.say: Stand next to a tree and look up. Now imagine a tree taller than the Statue of Liberty! Look at the bars: some of the tallest trees on Earth, with a house for size.

items.label: Hyperion (redwood)
items.ask: What is the tallest tree in the world?

explain.say: Look at the first bar: Hyperion, a coast redwood in California, USA, about 116 metres tall, the tallest known tree in the world. Its exact spot is kept secret to protect it. Can you find the Statue of Liberty?

items.label: Hyperion (redwood)
items.ask: What is the tallest tree in the world?

explain.say: There it is, 93 metres from the ground to the torch. Look: three trees beat it! Menara, a yellow meranti tree in Borneo, is the tallest tropical tree, and Centurion in Tasmania, Australia, is the tallest eucalyptus. Which tree is shorter than the statue?

items.label: Hyperion (redwood)
items.ask: What is the tallest tree in the world?

explain.say: General Sherman! It is not the tallest, but look how thick it is: a giant sequoia in California, it is the biggest tree on Earth by size, its trunk holds about 1,500 cubic metres of wood, enough to fill more than half an Olympic swimming pool.

draw.verdict: Tallest is not the same as biggest

explain.say: Brilliant! Look at the verdict: tallest is not the same as biggest. Wow fact: a bristlecone pine called Methuselah, in California, is over 4,800 years old, older than the Great Pyramid!

faq.q: What is the tallest tree in the world?
faq.a: Hyperion, a coast redwood in Redwood National Park, California, about 116 metres tall. It was found in 2006.
General Sherman, a giant sequoia in California, is the largest single tree by volume, about 1,500 cubic metres of wood, and about 84 metres tall.

faq.q: How old is the oldest tree?
faq.a: A Great Basin bristlecone pine named Methuselah, in California, is more than 4,800 years old.

faq.q: What is the tallest tropical tree?
faq.a: Menara, a yellow meranti tree in Sabah, Borneo, Malaysia, measured at about 100.8 metres in 2019.

faq.q: Why are some trees so tall?
faq.a: Coast redwoods get lots of rain and fog, have deep soil and few strong winds, and grow for hundreds of years, so they keep reaching up for sunlight.
asks: How do trees grow so tall?

facts: Hyperion, a coast redwood, is about 116 metres tall, the tallest known living tree.
General Sherman, a giant sequoia, is the largest known single-stem tree by volume.
Methuselah, a Great Basin bristlecone pine, is over 4,800 years old.
